OH WAIT. I see it! In `handle`, when the primal is infeasible, we call solve_infeasible. But in diag2 I called `P.solve_infeasible(prob)` after `P.solve_optimal(prob)` returned None. Let me re-run diag2 and print which candidate was chosen, plus the score.

Hmm, actually, maybe the issue is the *scoring*: `cand = (score, maxabs, y, q)` and comparison `(cand[0], cand[1]) < (best[0], best[1])`. If the min-norm candidate has score 0 but the margin candidate has score 0 too and a *smaller* maxabs... no, the margin one had maxabs 1e7.

Hmm, wait. Maybe the issue is that the min-norm candidate was REJECTED because `val <= 0`?! Let's see: for the min-norm LP, the returned z satisfies b^T y + d^T q = 1 (equality constraint). val should be 1. Unless the equality was violated...

Hmm, or maybe the rescale: `if abs(val - 1.0) > 1e-9: y = y/val` — fine.

cd /app/work && cat > diag4.py <<'PYEOF'
import json, sys, numpy as np
from scipy import sparse
from scipy.optimize import linprog
sys.path.insert(0,'/app/work'); sys.path.insert(0,'/app/submission')
import gen as G, check as C
import planner as P
seed=int(sys.argv[1])
r=G.gen(seed)
req=P.parse_request(json.dumps(r).encode())
prob=P.Problem(req)
R,K,n=prob.R,prob.K,prob.n
core=P._farkas_core(prob)
top=sparse.hstack([core, sparse.csr_matrix((n,1))],format="csr")
yrows=sparse.hstack([-sparse.eye(R,format="csr"), sparse.csr_matrix((R,K)), -sparse.csr_matrix(np.ones((R,1)))],format="csr")
qrows=sparse.hstack([sparse.csr_matrix((2*K,R)), sparse.vstack([sparse.eye(K),-sparse.eye(K)],format="csr"), -sparse.csr_matrix(np.ones((2*K,1)))],format="csr")
M_ub=sparse.vstack([top,yrows,qrows],format="csr")
b_ub=np.zeros(n+R+2*K)
A_eq=sparse.csr_matrix(np.concatenate([prob.b,prob.d,[0.0]])[None,:])
bounds=[(None,0.0)]*R+[(None,None)]*K+[(0.0,1e7)]
obj=np.zeros(R+K+1); obj[-1]=1.0
res=linprog(obj,A_ub=M_ub,b_ub=b_ub,A_eq=A_eq,b_eq=[1.0],bounds=bounds,method="highs")
z=np.array(res.x)
y=z[:R]; q=z[R:R+K]
val=float(prob.b.dot(y))+float(prob.d.dot(q))
print("val", val, "w", z[-1])
col=P._dense_cols(prob,y,q)
print("max col", col.max(), "max y", y.max())
print("norm after rescale", np.max(np.abs(y/val)), np.max(np.abs(q/val)))
print("planner result:", np.max(np.abs(P.solve_infeasible(prob)[0])))
PYEOF
